name: GET /api/leadflow/analytics/funnel - rates by source, nothing hidden
description:
Contact, booking, show and win rates by source, with pipeline health and onboarding attainment.

POOR SOURCES ARE SURFACED, NEVER FILTERED (51fff16e-dedb-4033-9d19-afebdccd41c2#AC3). SOP §20 says so in as many words, and the temptation runs the other way: a source with 400 leads and 2 meetings makes the dashboard look bad, and the natural instinct is a minimum-conversion filter that quietly hides it. That filter is exactly how a bad channel keeps getting budget. So the query has no HAVING clause on conversion and every source is returned; poor_quality is a RANKING over the same set, not a subset that replaces it.

RANKED BY WASTED VOLUME rather than by conversion percentage. A source with three leads and no wins has a 0% rate and costs nothing; one with four hundred leads and two wins has a 0.5% rate and is where the money is going - sorting by rate alone puts the harmless one first.

ONBOARDING ATTAINMENT IS MEASURED AGAINST THE ONE-BUSINESS-DAY STANDARD (51fff16e-dedb-4033-9d19-afebdccd41c2#AC4), not against "eventually": a handoff accepted in six days met the goal on any measure that only asks whether it happened.

The two hard pipeline targets - zero unowned and zero active-without-NEXT - are reported as raw counts rather than percentages, because 99.4% owned sounds like success and is forty leads nobody is working. QA: measured live over 90 days across seven real sources.

testCases.name: Every source is returned, with poor performers ranked rather than removed
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
